info.title: mousewheeld
info.description:
The locomotion input of a braemons rig: a running wheel, read and published.

Units are in the names — `position_cm`, `counts_per_cm`, `velocity_cm_s`. Counts are the device's only unit; everything that leaves here is centimetres. Unknown fields are refused rather than defaulted.

put.summary: Change a calibration by hand. Every field optional; the rest is left alone.

get.summary: The 2-D skeleton: modelled, routed, and refused by name.

post.summary: Make the measurement the rig's truth.

Stop counting and report — measured beside configured, and what the
difference looks like.
Note the counter and start counting.

get.summary: What board is attached, and how the link behaves.

post.summary: Open the link, or say why not.

get.summary: What the board runs, and what this daemon could put on it.

The wire's recent past: the whole conversation, and the last hundred
samples.
get.description:
A monitor that started at "now" would miss every fault that had already
happened, which is most of them — so the ring is handed over first and the
stream follows it. Samples are capped rather than the conversation, because
at 500 Hz they are the only thing that would come back.

get.summary:
The output line map, as the rig config describes it. Not writable: see the
module note.

post.summary: Move the API origin — never the accumulator a camera differences.

get.summary:
Per axis: counts, position, distance, both velocities. Plus whether the
link is still delivering, because everything above is only as true as that.
What this daemon is, and what it speaks.
get.description:
**Advertised, never gated.** A client that needs a field added last month
asks this first; a daemon that refused an older client's request on the
strength of a version would make every upgrade a coordinated one.

Write a set to the store. Stored as authored — `$name` references intact,
centimetres intact — because the store is what a person edits and copies
between rigs. Compilation happens at arm.

This is what lets a zone set be wrong in an editor rather than at arm time,
which is the difference between a message on screen and a TTL that fires in
the wrong place in the middle of a session.

ApiErrorBody.description: A refusal, as the API renders it.

context.description:
What to change: a zone set's name, the field that did not fit. May be
empty when the sentence is the whole story.

ArmOrigin.description: Where the metric is measured from.

label.description:
Opaque text stored with the arm — triald writes `trial 42`. The daemon
stays trial-blind and hands it back unread.

patch.description: Per-trial values for this set's `$name` bounds.

zone_set.description:
A name from the store. Never a slot: the daemon holds the sets, and a
name it does not have is a configuration error the caller can report.

ArmedZones.description: `GET /api/zones` — what is armed, what fired, when.

AxisCalibration.description: One axis' calibration, as the rig config stores it and the API returns it.

counts_per_cm.description:
Counts per centimetre of travel at the running surface. The number that
converts the device's only unit into everybody else's.

counts_per_rev.description:
Encoder counts per revolution, after quadrature ×4. Kept for the
arithmetic a measurement is checked against — a whole-number ratio
between the two is a decoder counting ×1 or ×2, not a wheel of the wrong
size.

diameter_cm.description:
The wheel's diameter — a full extent, never a radius. Porting from a
package that specifies radii means doubling at the boundary.

invert.description:
Count the other way. Applied by the device to its own accumulator, so
everything downstream reads a wheel that turns forwards.

measured_at.description:
When `counts_per_cm` was last measured rather than computed. `None` is
not a missing field: it means nobody has ever rolled this wheel against
a tape, and the panels say so.

name.description: The axis this describes, matching the axis names everywhere else.

AxisCalibrationPatch.description: A change to one axis: everything optional, so a panel can send one field.

counts.description: The device's 64-bit accumulator. The only unit the firmware knows.

device_velocity_cm_s.description:
As the device reported it: counts over a fixed window in its scan, at
scan resolution. Coarser, and the one the analog output and the zone
evaluation were actually done against.

distance_cm.description: Direction-free odometer since the origin was last moved.

velocity_cm_s.description: Computed by the host from the sample path.

BallCalibration.description: Declared, refused, and here so the shape of the answer is not a surprise.

sensor_angles_deg.description: Where each sensor sits, in degrees around the ball.

Calibration.description: Every axis' calibration, plus the 2-D skeleton.

oneOf.description:
The ball's transform — sensor mounting angle, ball diameter, the map
onto `x`, `y` and `yaw`. Always `None` today; its routes answer 501. It
exists in the model so that adding the hardware is filling in rather
than redesigning.

scan_hz.description: The scan the firmware runs its counters and zones at.

ConfigView.description:
`GET /api/config` — the settings a session may change, and the ones it may
only read, in one answer.

port.description: Read-only here: wiring is changed where wiring is described.

shm_open.description:
Whether that segment is actually open. A name in a config file and a
mapped segment are different things, and the difference is the whole
reason a corridor sometimes does not move.

shm_writes.description: Writes that have reached it since it was created.

starves_the_display.description: True when `rate_hz` is at or below `display_hz`.

oneOf.description:
The set written to the board's flash, if any: a standalone rig comes up
with its zones, and the board reports which copy it holds.

port.description: The serial port this daemon owns, from the rig config.

protocol_version.description: The wire protocol version the board greeted with.

uptime_device_us.description:
The board's clock since it booted — a reset shows up here before it
shows up anywhere else.

board.description: What the attached board greeted with, if one has.

floor.description:
The oldest it will talk to. Below this a board is refused by name rather
than half-understood.

FireRule.description: What happens after a zone fires.

available.description: What this daemon ships and could flash. Empty until the firmware exists.

running.description: What the attached board is running.

LinkHealth.description: Whether what the rest of this answer says can be believed.

measured_rate_hz.description:
What the samples are actually arriving at, as opposed to what was asked
for. The two differing is the finding.

ring_drops.description: The device's own rings overflowed: the firmware telling on itself.

seq_gaps.description:
Samples the daemon never received. **A path with a hole in it says so**
rather than reporting a shorter distance that looks complete.

stale.description:
No sample for longer than the staleness window. Everything above is the
last thing that was true.

connection_count.description:
How many times this daemon has (re)connected to a board. A number that
climbs on its own is a cable.

last_error.description: The last thing the board refused, kept because it is usually the answer.

zone_sets_invalidated.description:
Compiled zone sets are stale now, and the next arm recompiles. A set
armed under one calibration is never silently reinterpreted under
another.

MeasurementResult.description:
What the wheel said, beside what the config says. Never applied on its own:
a calibration change invalidates every compiled zone set, so it is a second,
deliberate press.

decoding_suspect.description:
Set when the measurement is a whole-number multiple of the configured
value: a decoding mistake rather than a wheel, and worth saying in
words before somebody applies it.

implied_circumference_cm.description:
The circumference the measurement implies, when the counts per
revolution are known — the number to hold against the wheel with a tape.

nominal_counts_per_cm.description:
What the wheel's stated dimensions imply — the arithmetic this
measurement exists to correct. On the report rather than left to a
client, so a result is readable on its own a month later.

counts_at_start.description:
The counter when counting began, so a UI can show progress without
asking the daemon to keep a second copy of it.

OutputAction.description: How the line behaves while the condition holds.

index.description:
The board's own index for this line — what the wire carries, since the
protocol is indices and not names.

name.description: What a zone set calls it.

pin.description: The pin it is wired to, on this board.

safe_high.description:
The level the firmware drives when nothing else says otherwise. Outputs
reach this before anything else runs.

device_us.description: The device clock. Correlating it with the host's is the daemon's job.

host_monotonic_ns.description:
`CLOCK_MONOTONIC` nanoseconds — the join key with statemachined's trace
and vstimd's vblank timestamps.

lost_before.description:
Samples the daemon **never received** since the previous frame on this
socket, accumulated across the ones decimation dropped. Only the daemon
can tell decimation from loss; a consumer breaks its line on this and on
nothing else.

seq.description:
The device's own sample counter. **Not a loss signal for a consumer**:
this stream is decimated, so `seq` skips by design. See `lost_before`.

known_distance_cm.description:
How far the wheel is about to be rolled, by hand, along its running
surface. A metre in one continuous motion: a metre averages away where
you started and stopped, and one revolution does not.

counts_per_cm.description:
The calibration it was compiled against, so a report is readable a day
later without guessing which one was in force.

problem.description:
The first thing wrong, in the words the compiler would use. `None` when
it compiles.

references.description: The `$name`s this set still needs at arm time.

api.description:
The API contract's major version. Within it, changes are additive:
fields, routes and enum values may appear; nothing is removed, renamed
or given a new meaning.

daemon.description: This daemon's release, from the build.

vinput_layout.description:
The `vinput` segment layout this daemon writes — the one interface in
the family where a mismatch is bytes reinterpreted rather than a field
gone missing, and therefore the one that is checked rather than
advertised. The reader refuses to map a segment whose version is not its
own; this is here so a person can see why before it happens.

WireLine.description: One line of the wire, either direction, uninterpreted.

ZeroRequest.description:
`POST /api/position/zero`.

Moves the **API origin** — what displacement, distance and the zones are
measured from. Never the accumulator published to a camera: vstimd
differences that every frame, and a value that jumps backwards jumps the
corridor backwards. Teleporting a corridor is a command to vstimd, from
whoever runs the experiment.

axes.description: Which axes. Empty means all of them.

The axes this zone constrains, in the order its bounds are given. One
for a wheel; a 2-D rectangle on a ball is already expressible.

level.description:
Fire on arming if the animal is already inside. Off by default: a zone
fires on the false→true **edge** of "inside", so arming a zone somebody
is standing in does not fire it.

max_cm.description: The high end per axis. `null` is open.

min_cm.description: The low end per axis, in the order of `axes`.

wrap_cm.description: A circular track: the metric is evaluated modulo this period.

oneOf.description: "$name", resolved from the patch given at arm time
an open bound: everything past the other end

ZoneBound.description: One end of a zone's interval on one axis.

ZoneMetric.description: Which quantity a zone is compared against.

line.description: A **name** from the rig config's line map, never a pin number.

ms.description: Pulse width. Ignored by a `level` output.

ZoneSet.description:
A named set, as it is stored and as it is uploaded.

Declaration order resolves two zones firing in one scan: both still fire,
and the order is the order of their `zone_hit` messages.

zone_set_version.description:
Bumped by whoever edits the set. The board reports the version it holds,
so "is the board running what I think it is" is one comparison.

ZoneShape.description:
The only shape today, and a discriminator rather than a flag: a future
`circle` or `polygon` is a new value, and a shape the firmware does not know
is refused whole rather than half-evaluated.

ZoneStatus.description:
What a zone is doing right now.

The bounds are **as armed**, in centimetres: the `$name`s resolved from the
trial's patch and the counts the board is actually comparing against,
converted back. Without them a UI can only draw the set as *stored*, which
for a parameterised set is a picture of a zone that is not the one running —
and "is the reward region where I think it is" is the question the picture
exists to answer.

min_cm.description: Per axis, in the order the zone names them. `null` is an open bound.

wrap_cm.description: The period the metric is taken modulo, if the zone wraps.
